facts.statement: The species name honors Daniel Mesa, a local shepherd who found the fossil while looking for lost sheep.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Daniel Mesa, a local shepherd who discovered the specimen while searching for lost sheep.

facts.statement: The only known specimen was found in the Cañadón Calcáreo Formation, about 25 km north-northeast of Cerro Cóndor in Chubut Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: The holotype and only known specimen (Museo Paleontológico Egidio Feruglio MPEF-PV 1716) was collected from an erosional exposure of fluvial sandstone within the Cañadón Calcáreo Formation on a hill approximately 25 km north-northeast of Cerro Cóndor, Chubut Province, in west-central Argentina, South America.

facts.statement: Brachytrachelopan lived in Argentina during the Late Jurassic, specifically from the Oxfordian to Tithonian stages.
facts.quote: Brachytrachelopan is a genus of short-necked sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian to Tithonian) of Argentina.

facts.statement: Brachytrachelopan was small for a sauropod, measuring 10 to 11 meters in length and 5 metric tons in body mass.
facts.quote: Small for a sauropod, Brachytrachelopan measured 10 - 11 m in length and 5 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: Researchers determined the specimen was an adult, not a juvenile, based on the high degree of fusion between neural arches and centra.
facts.quote: Rauhut et al. (2005, 670) note that the high degree of fusion present between the preserved neural arches and their respective centra, as well as fusion between the sacral centra, sacral neural arches, and sacral neural spines is evidence that the holotype does not represent a juvenile animal.

facts.statement: The neck structure suggests Brachytrachelopan specialized in eating plants growing at heights between 1 and 2 meters.
facts.quote: Moreover, the morphology of the cervical neural arches in Brachytrachelopan would have significantly restricted dorsal flexion of the neck and most likely indicates that this sauropod was specialized to a diet of plants "growing at heights of between about 1 and 2 m."

facts.statement: Brachytrachelopan is classified within the family Dicraeosauridae, the group Diplodocoidea, and the suborder Neosauropoda.
facts.quote: Brachytrachelopan belongs to Sauropoda and Neosauropoda from the group of Diplodocoidea and family Dicraeosauridae.

facts.statement: Rauhut and colleagues proposed that Brachytrachelopan is more closely related to the Late Jurassic African Dicraeosaurus than to the Lower Cretaceous South American Amargasaurus.
facts.quote: Rauhut et al. (2005, 671-672; Fig. 2) assigned Brachytrachelopan to the Dicraeosauridae, proposing that, within this clade, it should be considered to have a sister group relationship to the Late Jurassic African taxon Dicraeosaurus, instead of to Amargasaurus from the Lower Cretaceous of South America.

facts.statement: Brachytrachelopan is distinguished by cervical vertebrae that are as long as or shorter than they are high, plus unique features like pillar-like laminae and anteriorly flexed neural spine tips.
facts.quote: Rauhut et al. (2005, 670) diagnose Brachytrachelopan as differing from all other sauropods in the following respects: "...individual cervical vertebrae being as long as, or shorter in anteroposterior length than, high posteriorly. Further apomorphies...include a pronounced, pillar-like centropostzygapophyseal lamina in the cervical vertebrae, a pronounced anterior inclination in the mid-cervical neural spines, with the tip of the spine extending beyond the anterior end of the centrum, and anterior dorsal neural spines one to six with vertical bases and anteriorly flexed tips."

facts.statement: Brachytrachelopan breaks several supposed sauropod characteristics by being small in size and having a notably short neck compared to other sauropods.
facts.quote: Brachytrachelopan rompe con varias supuestas características sobre los saurópodos, ya que era de un pequeño tamaño y su cuello era notablemente corto si lo comparamos con los otros saurópodos.

facts.statement: Brachytrachelopan was an unusual sauropod with a short neck and a total length of 10 meters.
facts.quote: Brachytrachelopan es un inusual saurópodo de cuello corto de solo 10 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Its neck was approximately 40% shorter than other dicraeosaurids and the shortest of all known sauropods.
facts.quote: Su cuello era aproximadamente un 40 % más corto que el de los otros dicreosáuridos y el más corto de todos los saurópodos conocidos.

facts.statement: The estimated length of its neck was 1.1 meters.
facts.quote: Su longitud se estima en 1,1 metros.

facts.statement: The neck consisted of 12 vertebrae that were much shorter than those found in other known sauropods.
facts.quote: Este cuello tenía 12 vértebras, pero estas eran mucho más cortas que las comunes encontradas en otros saurópodos conocidos.

facts.statement: The vertebrae exhibited a strongly opisthocoelous form, where individual vertebrae were convex anteriorly and concave posteriorly.
facts.quote: La forma de las vértebras es fuertemente opistocélica, un patrón de articulación vertebral en el que las vértebras individuales son convexas anteriores y cóncavas posteriormente.

facts.statement: The longest vertebral centrum measured only 10 centimeters.
facts.quote: El centro vertebral más largo solo medía 10 centímetros.

facts.statement: It likely fed on vegetation at a height of 1 to 2 meters and may have been very selective in choosing its food.
facts.quote: Probablemente se alimentaba de la vegetación a una altura de 1 a 2 metros, siendo posible que fuese muy selectivo en elegir sus alimentos.

facts.statement: Fossil remains were found by Daniel Mesa, a sheep herder looking for lost animals, who marked the spot with a stake.
facts.quote: Los restos fósiles de Brachytrachelopan fueron encontrados por Daniel Mesa, un pastor de ovejas que buscaba algunos animales perdidos, y que marcó el lugar con una estaca.

facts.statement: The fossils date to the Tithonian, approximately 150 million years ago.
facts.quote: que data del Titoniano, hace 150 millones de años atrás.

facts.statement: The research team was led by German paleontologist Oliver Rauhut, working with Argentines Gerardo Cladera and Pablo Puerta.
facts.quote: El equipo fue encabezado por el paleontólogo alemán Oliver Rauhut, con quien trabajaron los argentinos Gerardo Cladera y Pablo Puerta.

facts.statement: The genus name translates to "Short-necked Pan," referencing the discoverer, a shepherd, and the dinosaur's notable short neck.
facts.quote: El género se traduce como "Pan de cuello corto", haciendo referencia al trabajo de quien descubriera los restos, ya que Pan es el dios griego de los pastores y a la notable característica del dinosaurio.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that due to its neck length, it may have had a very different lifestyle from those with longer necks, occupying an ecological niche not filled by its infraorder companions.
facts.quote: A raíz de la longitud de su cuello, se plantea que pudo haber presentado un estilo de vida muy distinto a los que poseían un cuello más largo, ocupando un nicho ecológico que sus compañeros de infraorden no ocuparon.

facts.statement: The spinous processes of the spine include a prespinal, postspinal, spinocigapophysial plate, and lateral spinopostcigapophysial laminae, otherwise possessing shorter spinodiapophysial processes.
facts.quote: Las apófisis espinosas de la columna vertebral comprende la siguiente placa, prespinal, postespinal, espinocigapofisial y láminas espinopostcigapofisial laterales, de lo contrario, poseen procesos espinodiapofisial más corto.

facts.statement: Brachytrachelopan lived in what is now Patagonia during the late Jurassic, approximately 150 million years ago.
facts.quote: Brachytrachelopan vivió zonas en lo que es hoy la Patagonia, al final del período Jurásico, hace 150 millones de años.

facts.statement: Brachytrachelopan was a herbivore.
facts.quote: Brachytrachelopan es un herbívoro.

facts.statement: The geological formation containing Brachytrachelopan fossils consists of river sediments, with evidence of lakes and swamps in the lower layers.
facts.quote: En la formación geológica, de la que provienen sus restos se formaron a partir de sedimentos de un río, aunque en la parte inferior se ve también el impacto de lagos y pantanos.

facts.statement: The dominant plants in Brachytrachelopan's environment included Classopollis, Callialasporites, and Cyclusphaera.
facts.quote: Entre las plantas dominaban los Classopollis y Callialasporites, y Cyclusphaera.

facts.statement: Brachytrachelopan belongs to the parent group Dicraeosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Dicraeosaurinae

facts.statement: Brachytrachelopan is classified in the family Dicraeosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Dicraeosauridae

facts.statement: Brachytrachelopan is a member of the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Brachytrachelopan lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian stages, between 154.8 and 145.06 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (154.8 to 145.06 million years ago)

facts.statement: While a hypothesis links sauropod neck elongation to sexual selection, this view is refuted by other authors.
facts.quote: aunque hay una segunda hipótesis que lo asocia a efectos de la selección sexual, que esta última es refutada por otros autores.
